title: Migration rehearsal sizes the budget transfer as a fraction of a hard-coded CONSTANT rather than of the actual balance — moves 88.67%, not the documented 90%, and strands 345 phUSD in three untracked contracts
propagation: LOCAL-ONLY (but the formula must never be ported — see differential-gap.md §3.1)
specText: Autonomous Decision #4 (story lines ~604-615): 'initiateMigration() runs FIRST (it settles and freezes, making committedDebt final), then a constant 90% of REHEARSAL_STAKER_BUDGET is moved to V2. The amount is a constant rather than balanceOf(v1) - committedDebt() because a forge script builds its calldata during the simulation pass, where all rehearsal transactions share one timestamp and committedDebt reads 0; the broadcast then replays that stale number against a chain where it is non-zero. 90% is safe by ~7 orders of magnitude against a 12-month depletion window.' / 'Carry to story 072: mainnet Phase 6 must apply the same reordering.' Corroborated by the story's own embedded review, Issue 2: 'the rehearsal proves the *ordering* correction and nothing about sizing, so story 072 must inherit the sizing problem as unsolved, not as solved-per-docblock.'
description: `uint256 movable = (REHEARSAL_STAKER_BUDGET * 90) / 100;` computes 90% of a hard-coded seed constant, not 90% of the staker's actual phUSD balance. Between the `topUp(REHEARSAL_STAKER_BUDGET)` at :1734 and the migration, the three seed NFT mints route through the Uniboost donation branch and the UniboostMintDebtHook mints additional phUSD INTO the V1 staker. That contribution is excluded from the transfer entirely. The in-source comment at :1822-1830 describes the result as 'a flat 90%' and ':1788' says it 'leaves an arbitrary 10% stranded' — both understate the divergence.
impact: Measured on the live chain: V1 actual balance 1015.014 phUSD, moved 900, so the actual fraction moved is 88.67% and the stranded residual is 115.014 phUSD (11.33%) per staker — 345.042 phUSD across the three. The post-condition at :1712 (`phUSD.balanceOf(v2) > 0`) cannot detect this: it proves non-zero, not correctly-sized. On mainnet, where the mint-debt hook has been minting into the live stakers for months, the seed constant would be an arbitrary and possibly small fraction of the real balance, so 'flat 90%' could move almost any proportion. The author explicitly disclaims the number (:1783-1789: 'Do not read this 90% as a validated answer; the rehearsal proves nothing about sizing') and hands sizing to story 072 as OPEN.
attackPath: No attack path. Intent-mismatch: `(REHEARSAL_STAKER_BUDGET * 90) / 100` sizes the move from a hard-coded seed constant instead of the staker's live balance, so the realised fraction is 88.67%, not the 'flat 90%' the in-source comments at :1822-1830 and :1788 claim.
evidence: cast against the deployed chain: three V1 stakers at 0x976fcd02…, 0x413b1afc…, 0x359570b3… hold 115.014007236759570733 / 115.014007236826930907 / 115.014039422670157249 phUSD after migration; the three V2 stakers each hold exactly 900e18 with totalStaked == 3. Staker #3 additionally ended with committedDebt == 1 wei (the others 0), directly confirming the accrual-during-broadcast effect the constant works around is real. None of the six rehearsal artifacts is tracked, so the stranded value is invisible to progress.31337.json, local.json, addresses.ts and the :3001 API.
recommendation: For the mainnet port: compute `balance - committedDebt` at execution time, or move the budget in a separate transaction after `initiateMigration` has frozen `committedDebt`. The forge simulate-then-replay defect that forced the constant does not apply on mainnet, where every `*:broadcast` npm entry uses `--skip-simulation`. Port the ORDERING finding the rehearsal exists to produce (settle+freeze before moving the budget, :1778-1781); do not port the number. Locally, either track the rehearsal artifacts or assert the residual explicitly.

severityRationale: QA (DOWNGRADED from Low). The faithfulness re-run resolves the axis this finding was originally weighed on, and it resolves it IN THE CODE'S FAVOUR. (1) THE CODE IS FAITHFUL. Autonomous Decision #4 does not merely tolerate the constant, it MANDATES it: 'a constant 90% of REHEARSAL_STAKER_BUDGET is moved to V2 ... rather than balanceOf(v1) - committedDebt()', with a sound and independently-verifiable technical reason (a forge script builds calldata in the simulation pass where all rehearsal transactions share one timestamp, so committedDebt reads 0 and the broadcast replays a stale number). `movable = (REHEARSAL_STAKER_BUDGET * 90) / 100` is exactly what AD#4 specifies. There is no deviation to report under Law 2, so `faithfulness` is FALSE by test rather than by omission. (2) THE DIVERGENCE IS IN THE SAFE DIRECTION. The 88.67% arises because the UniboostMintDebtHook mints ~15 phUSD INTO the V1 staker after the topUp - phUSD the constant excludes. Moving a fraction of the constant therefore moves strictly LESS than 90% of the live balance, i.e. it is strictly MORE conservative than the documented intent and cannot breach `committedDebt`. A deviation whose only direction is safer is not a spec violation with impact; it is an imprecise comment. (3) THE SIZING QUESTION IS FLAGGED OPEN, NOT CONCEALED. The docblock marks sizing UNSOLVED and inherits it to story 072, and the story's own review independently reaffirms 'the rehearsal proves the ordering correction and nothing about sizing'. Under this repo's standards a disclosed open design question is not an audit finding against the implementation. WHAT REMAINS, and why it is not dropped to nothing: the 345.042 phUSD stranded across three UNTRACKED rehearsal contracts is a true local state-handling artifact (invisible to progress.31337.json, local.json, addresses.ts and the :3001 API), and the in-source docblock's 'flat 90%' wording is inaccurate on numbers the story's own review already had to correct once (:1722-1728 vs :1772). State handling and incorrect comments are the literal C4 QA definition. MUST NOT BE FLATTENED INTO QA-BUNDLE NOISE: the actionable content survives the downgrade unchanged and is the reason this entry exists at all - for the mainnet port, carry the ORDERING lesson (settle+freeze before moving the budget) and NEVER the number; compute `balance - committedDebt` at execution time, which is available on mainnet because every `*:broadcast` npm entry uses `--skip-simulation` and the forge simulate-then-replay defect that forced the constant therefore does not apply. The LOCAL-ONLY propagation flag is deliberately UNCHANGED by this downgrade.
severityAgreement: DOWNGRADED low -> qa on the faithfulness re-run. The faithfulness axis was TESTED and CLEARED (not merely unexamined).

reweigh.basis: AD#4 explicitly mandates the constant-derived sizing and gives a sound technical reason; the realised fraction errs conservative; sizing is disclosed-open and inherited by story 072. Faithfulness axis tested and cleared.

parkedItemsCarriedForward.title: ERC4626YieldStrategy.previewRedeem / previewDeposit view passthroughs still STATICCALL the underlying vault — the story-060 / YS-01 Tokemak fix is one-directional
parkedItemsCarriedForward.sourceVerification: Read against the TOP-LEVEL submodule HEAD lib/reflax-yield-vault (not a nested stale pin). :73-75 `return vault.previewDeposit(assets);` and :83-85 `return vault.previewRedeem(shares);`, both declared `external view` => Solidity emits STATICCALL. Twenty lines below, :110-115 credits principal via `vault.convertToAssets(sharesReceived)` with an in-source comment naming the exact hazard: 'Use convertToAssets (NOT previewRedeem): convertToAssets is ERC4626-mandated STATICCALL-safe, whereas some real vaults (e.g. Tokemak Autopools) mutate state inside previewRedeem and revert with StateChangeDuringStaticCall when called as an external view.' The authors therefore knew the hazard and hardened ONE call site.
parkedItemsCarriedForward.whyItMatters: Against a real Tokemak Autopool these two views revert for every caller, always; against MockAutoDOLA (plain un-overridden OZ ERC4626) they return a clean number, always. The local rig therefore reports green on the exact behaviour that already bricked this project's YS-swap suite. Blast radius today is UI/keeper reads (no first-party on-chain caller found), which is why this is parked for triage rather than asserted as a Medium.

secondaryGapsInTheSameMockSection: No maxRedeem/maxWithdraw check before `vault.redeem` in _disposeShares (:128-135): against a real Autopool with a liquid reserve below the request, user withdrawals brick. Locally impossible to reproduce.

MockAutoDOLA._updateYield() mints assets into the vault BEFORE super._deposit mints shares, so convertToAssets(sharesReceived) > amount and creditedPrincipal at :115 can EXCEED the deposited amount — the precise opposite of that line's stated intent. Any local invariant asserting 'principal is never over-credited' passes VACUOUSLY. Flagged because a vacuous-harness result is a known repeat failure mode in this repo.
